answer: The owner device sends signed heartbeat attestations on a schedule, and the dead-man switch fires only after a run of missed heartbeats. Each heartbeat is a fresh signature that cannot be replayed, so an attacker cannot fake continued life. Keeping many fake identities alive means generating genuine heartbeats for each, one by one. The system restores a comet only after its credentials survive the challenge. A plume alone is noise; a island of verified recoveries is a continuity the network can trust.
